CANCER THERAPY
Introduction
Cancer is abnormal and rapid cell growth with the potential to invade near or
distant organs. It is the 2 nd leading cause of death globally. Common adult
cancers occur in the lung, breast, colon and rectum, liver, cervix, prostate and
the ovaries. Some childhood cancers are leukaemias, lymphomas, Wilm's
tumour, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma and retinoblastoma. This section
focuses mainly on adult tumours.
Risk factors
Genetics, family history, occupational exposures (radiation exposure and
hydrocarbons) tobacco, obesity, alcohol, certain infections
Classification
- Based on tissue of origin
- Carcinomas are derived from epithelial cells
- Sarcomas are derived from mesenchymal cells (bone, cartilage, muscle,
fat, nerve, etc.)
- Lymphomas / Leukaemias are derived from blood forming cells
- Blastomas are derived from embryonic cells
- Germ cell tumours are derived from pluripotent cells
